title: Fin Box Root Rib — Crack Stop and Reinforcing Plate Repair at the Lower Load Introduction

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Interim crack stop and reinforcing plate repair at the fin box root rib lower load introduction, used to return an aircraft to service after a crack finding while a permanent reinforcement is planned.

sections.purpose: This repair arrests a crack at the fin box root rib lower load introduction and restores the local load path with a bolted reinforcing plate, as an interim measure with a defined life.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish both crack tips by high frequency eddy current and confirm them by dye penetrant after the sealant has been removed. Measure the crack length along the flange radius and record the station. A crack longer than the limit below, a crack that has turned into the web, or a second crack in the same station is outside the scope of this repair and the rib must be assessed by the design office before the aircraft is moved. Inspect the shear tie D5530110749890 at the same station and the splice plate D5530119339028 for secondary cracking; a crack in either makes this repair invalid. Record the aircraft flight cycles, because the repair life is expressed in cycles from the date of embodiment.
sections.repair_procedure: Drill the crack stop holes at both tips to the diameter on repair drawing RD-55-30-11-910, positioned so that the hole is centred on the tip and not short of it. Ream and cold work the holes to the instructions and confirm the finish. Do a dye penetrant inspection of both holes; an indication means the tip was not captured and the hole must be enlarged to the next size or the repair abandoned. Machine the reinforcing plate seat on the rib flange and prepare the faying surfaces. Apply the chromate-free protection to all bare material including the crack stop holes. Fit the strap D5530113880239 dry and check the gap with a feeler gauge over the whole footprint; shim any gap larger than the drawing value with a laminated shim and do not pull it out with the fasteners. Install the anchor nuts AES147323-7D in the rib flange to the pattern on the drawing. Install the fasteners wet with sealant, working outwards from the crack stop positions, and torque them in the sequence on sheet 2. Seal the plate edge and restore the protection scheme.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 9000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. A high frequency eddy current inspection of both crack stop holes and of the plate perimeter is required every 3000 flight cycles, with the rudder removed and the fin leading edge open. Any growth from a crack stop hole, any indication at the plate perimeter, or any loose anchor nut makes the repair invalid and the aircraft must not be released. Report every embodiment to Aeralis with the crack length and the station.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: A single crack up to 35 millimetres in length along the rib flange radius, not turned into the web, not closer than 25 millimetres to a fastener row and with no secondary cracking in the shear tie or the splice plate at the same station.

repair_drawings.title: Crack stop and reinforcing plate, fin box root rib lower station

type_data.fastener_pattern: Three rows, 36 fasteners, 22 mm pitch, 16 mm edge distance, with the outer row staggered across the flange radius
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 9000 flight cycles; a repeat high frequency eddy current inspection of the crack stop holes is required every 3000 flight cycles.
type_data.aerodynamic_smoothness: Class C, internal to the fin leading edge
